conceptName: Two front ends: the legacy shell and the Iapetus app

items.stem: How is SDM's user interface structured?

options.text: Two front ends — a legacy AngularJS shell and a newer Angular SPA at /Iapetus — both served by one backend
A desktop app plus a web app
Only server-rendered Razor pages, no JavaScript framework

items.explanation: SDM is mid-migration: the legacy AngularJS shell renders the outer page/menu, and newer screens are the Angular SPA mounted at /Iapetus — the same backend serves both.

misconceptions.a: There are two front ends, not one — older AngularJS and newer Angular 12.
misconceptions.c: Both front ends are web; there's no desktop client.
misconceptions.d: It uses Angular front ends; the Razor/MVC side is just the thin shell + SPA host.

items.stem: A menu link is marked "upgraded." What happens when you click it?

options.text: It loads the modern Angular SPA at /Iapetus/<feature>
It stays in the legacy AngularJS shell

items.explanation: An 'upgraded' link points at the new Angular app under /Iapetus; a non-upgraded (legacy) link renders in the old AngularJS shell.

misconceptions.b: That's a legacy (non-upgraded) link; upgraded links go to /Iapetus.
misconceptions.c: Upgraded links navigate to an app route, not a download.
misconceptions.d: Navigation doesn't sign the user out.

items.stem: Why does `/Iapetus` appear in the URL of the newer screens?

options.text: It's the SPA's mount path — the Angular app is built with base-href Iapetus and served there
It's the name of the database

items.explanation: The Angular SPA is mounted under /Iapetus (base-href Iapetus + the backend's IapetusController), so its routes live under that path.

misconceptions.d: The same backend serves it — not a separate server.

items.stem: Which statements about SDM's two front ends are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: One backend serves both the legacy shell and the Angular SPA
Features migrate from the legacy shell to the Angular app gradually
The legacy shell renders the outer page and the navigation menu
The two front ends run on two completely separate servers

items.explanation: A single backend hosts both; the legacy shell draws the page + menu; and features move to /Iapetus one at a time. They are not separately hosted.

misconceptions.d: Both are served by the same backend/origin, not separate servers.
